name: Medu Vada (Garelu)
instructions: 1. Soak urad dal in water for 4-6 hours, then drain.
2. Grind the dal into a thick, smooth batter using minimal ice-cold water; the texture should be light and fluffy.
3. Add finely chopped green chilies, ginger, cumin seeds, curry leaves, cilantro, salt, and onions (if using) to the batter and mix well.
4. Heat oil in a deep kadhai.
5. Wet your palms, take a small portion of the batter, shape it into a ball, flatten it, and poke a hole in the center to form a donut shape.
6. Carefully slide the vada into the hot oil.
7. Deep fry on medium heat, turning occasionally, until both sides are golden brown and crispy.
8. Serve hot with coconut chutney and sambar.
description: Garelu is a staple breakfast and festive delicacy in Andhra Pradesh. Often prepared during Vinayaka Chavithi and other traditional functions, these vadas are culturally significant as a popular offering to deities and a beloved comfort food served in most households and tiffin centers across the state.
